rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Never interpolate a credential variable with ${VAR:-fallback} in a liveness check; the :- form expands to the SECRET when set. Use ${VAR:+set}, and treat any command that names a token variable as a publishing action RECURRENCE of FM-96, 2026-08-15 14:12 EDT, committed by an agent that had FM-96 loaded in its context at the time. Checking GitHub auth before a push, the agent ran echo "GH_TOKEN: ${GH_TOKEN:+set}${GH_TOKEN:-UNSET}" intending to print set/UNSET. ${GH_TOKEN:-UNSET} expands to the VALUE when the variable is set, so the full ghs_ App installation token was printed to the transcript. The two idioms differ by one character and read identically at a glance. Evidence that a preloaded CRITICAL warning does not prevent the failure it describes: the entry was in-context and the operator was actively working ON the failure-mode registry. Audit triggered by this leak found 62 distinct ghs_ App tokens plus 5 distinct full-length long-lived credentials (2 gho_, 3 ghp_) across 14 transcript files dated 2026-07-23..2026-08-10; all full-length values scrubbed 2026-08-15, no rotation performed (founder decision, assumed dead). Mechanizable check: forbid the :- and :? forms on any variable whose name matches (TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL), and grep persisted transcripts for gh[pous]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36} as a post-session assertion.

rationale: filed at creation time

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Direct exit on a mid-flow refusal bypasses terminal-state machinery, stranding the lane In cli-dispatch's _cmd_start, a --continue-pr lane's destination_deliver() refusal (e.g. a foreign actor moving the PR's destination ref mid-run) caused the code to exit directly, bypassing the classify_terminal_state ladder and the delivered-transition -- the only two places that ever advance run_state/binding state out of running/active. destination_deliver() itself never transitions the binding on a refusal either. Result: a lane whose delivery failed after a successful managed-branch push was stranded forever with run_state=running, binding state=active. Fix (fleet#405/PR#539): write a terminal run_state and transition the binding to aborted before exiting on this path. General lesson: any early-exit added on a new failure path must be checked against whether it bypasses existing state-machine invariants, not just checked for the right exit code.

rationale: filed at creation time

rationale: filed at creation time

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Abort-path bookkeeping failure swallowed with || true, re-stranding the resource it was meant to protect fleet cli-dispatch's --continue-pr delivery-refusal handler calls lane_binding_transition(...) aborted || true before exit -- if the transition write itself fails, the || true discards that failure silently and the lane can be left in a non-terminal state exactly like the bug it was written to fix (fleet#405 round 2). This is the abort-path-is-load-bearing pattern: repairing an error path to 'do the right thing' still needs its own success to be checked, or the repair is cosmetic. Fix: check the transition's own exit status and escalate/log distinctly if it fails, rather than exit-swallowing a second layer deep.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A shared safety function (destination_deliver) wired for only one of two production callers, leaving the other silently unverified cli-dispatch's destination_deliver() -- the fail-closed function that pushes to a bound destination ref and verifies exact old-OID + fast-forward -- is gated at its only call site by [[ "$pushed" == "true" && -n "$continue_pr" && -n "$lane_id" ]]. The -n "$continue_pr" condition means start --onto NEVER reaches this block, even though --onto also sets a binding_destination and claims the same delivered-state guarantee. An --onto lane can report state=delivered while its destination ref was never pushed to, verified, or divergence-checked. destination_deliver() was added by fleet#404 explicitly 'dormant until #403' pending a caller wiring it up; fleet#405 wired it for --continue-pr only and never revisited --onto, and none of 6 same-vendor pev review rounds on #405 caught the gap in the sibling mode -- a genuine cross-vendor (Codex) audit did. General lesson: when a shared safety primitive is deliberately left dormant pending caller wiring, closing the loop for ONE caller does not retire the TODO -- grep all callers of the function/flag the primitive gates on before declaring the feature done, or the primitive's own docstring/comment should list every caller it must eventually cover.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Harness credential inherited at spawn, never re-synced (6th recurrence; recurrence of hc-FM-232) Long-lived non-interactive processes capture the GitHub App credential in their environment at spawn and hold it past its 1-hour TTL, while a freshly refreshed one sits in the on-disk cache beside them. The refresh hook rides on PROMPT_COMMAND, which is interactive-only, so background jobs, cron, and dispatched subagents never pick it up. Compounded twice: cron has no BASH_ENV so it inherits nothing at all, and cli-dispatch:5931 ADVISES falling back to a different identity on 401, encoding the violation in tooling. Measured 2026-08-15: the personal OAuth quota was driven to 0/5000 and re-drained to 0 within minutes of reset while the App pool sat at 7395/7500 unused. Downstream blast radius: starved lens agents returned null, which a vacuous merge gate (FM-285) then treated as unanimous PASS, so one dead credential produced unsound merges. Detection: check the rate-limit LIMIT, not the remaining (7500=App, 5000=OAuth); a 5000 in a session that believes it is on the App is proof it is not. Fix must be mechanical, not procedural: this is the 6th occurrence (2026-07-29, 07-30 x3, 08-10, 08-15) with a 100 percent miss rate for background sessions, and every prior occurrence closed by restating the rule. Fix the acquisition path and delete the advised fallback; per-harness refresh timers must exist for ALL harnesses (grok had none until 2026-08-15).

rationale: filed at creation time

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A shared credential-mint path must select the credential by DETECTED HARNESS with default-deny, never mint one harness credential unconditionally for every shell Measured 2026-08-15/16 (session 817d0e1f, CI-fleet audit): ~/.bash_env minted the Claude GitHub App installation token unconditionally on every non-interactive bash startup, so Codex-harness and Grok-harness processes inherited GH_TOKEN and authenticated to GitHub AS psimmons-claude-worker[bot]. Every commit, comment and API call they made was attributed to another harness, silently destroying the per-harness attribution that independent-review routing depends on (an agent could not tell it was borrowing an identity because gh auth status showed a valid App token). Detection: compare the acting bot login in a GitHub event against the harness that produced it; a single harness login across all harnesses is proof. Fix applied: route the mint on harness detection with default-deny (no harness detected = no token) rather than a single hardcoded harness. Related family: FM-292 (background/cron sessions falling through to founder OAuth) - same root surface (~/.bash_env + PROMPT_COMMAND refresh), different failure direction: FM-292 loses the App identity downward to OAuth, this one imposes ONE harness identity sideways onto all others.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A tool must never document a fallback that downgrades identity or authority as the remedy for its own auth error; remediation text inside tooling is an instruction, and it will be followed Measured 2026-08-15/16 (session 817d0e1f). cli-dispatch line 5931 advises operators and agents to retry with `env -u GH_TOKEN gh ...` when an App-token call returns 401. That silently swaps the GitHub App identity for the founder personal OAuth identity: the call then succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, while attribution moves to a human and the personal 5000/hr quota absorbs fleet traffic. Filed as fleet#546. The failure is not that an agent broke a rule - the rule (App tokens exclusively) was correctly recorded and repeatedly restated - it is that the TOOL taught the violation at exactly the moment of failure, when an agent is most likely to follow instructions verbatim. General check: grep tooling error paths and docs for remediation advice that removes a credential, lowers a permission, disables a check, or skips a gate; that advice is a defect, not documentation. Related: FM-292 records the same advice as one compounding cause of the 6th recurrence of OAuth quota starvation; this entry isolates the pattern so it is findable outside the GitHub-auth context.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A dispatch brief may not present unverified premises as KNOWN FACTS; every asserted fact in a brief is either carried with its verifying artifact or labelled a hypothesis to test Measured 2026-08-15/16 (session 817d0e1f, CI-fleet audit). A coordinator brief listed a KNOWN FACTS block; three of its entries were false and the executing agents spent budget falsifying them instead of doing the assigned work: (1) "armies CI has been failing for 4 months" - it had not; (2) "fleet-sync targets 404 because the repos were deleted" - they had been TRANSFERRED, not deleted; (3) "the telemetry units are instinct-project detritus" - zero overlap with instinct. One of the wrong root causes was published to fleet#549 before correction, so the error escaped the session into a public issue. Cost shape: a wrong fact in a brief is worse than an absent one, because the agent trusts it and reasons FORWARD from it, and the correction arrives only if the agent happens to trip over ground truth. Check: in any brief, each factual claim carries a command or artifact reference the executor can re-run in one step, or it is written as "unverified - confirm first".

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A failure mode recorded in an always-loaded file does not prevent its own recurrence; the standing rule it encodes must be enforced by a runtime gate or a dispatch-time check, not by being read Measured 2026-08-15/16 (session 817d0e1f). ~/HANDOFF.md - a file this session read at startup - already carried an entry from the fleet#405 work recording that Claude had personally authored every fix instead of dispatching Codex, violating the standing "Claude is QA, not builder" ruling. In this session I again personally authored the merge-gate fixes in ~/.claude/workflows (commits d407cfa, 4b05bf6, ffcd8ae, 0a4270f) rather than dispatching a builder. The prior occurrence was in context, in a file loaded before any work began, describing exactly the act about to be repeated. This is the same shape as FM-277 (an agent leaked a token while holding FM-96 in context) and cluster c-018: preloaded warnings have a measured miss rate near 100% at the moment of action, because the agent is attending to the task, not the registry. Check: for any rule of the form "role X must not do Y", place a mechanical gate at the point of action (a dispatch precondition, a pre-commit author check, a workflow step that refuses) - counting on the rule being loaded is not a control.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A defect proven fixed by a hand-run discriminating test is not closed until that test runs in an automatic path; an unwired proof expires the moment the session ends Measured 2026-08-15/16 (session 817d0e1f). Four merge-gate defects in ~/.claude/workflows were each proven by a discriminating test run by hand: pev.js returned MERGE on 0/3 lenses before d407cfa and BLOCKED after; pr-whole.js returned MERGE-READY on 0/3 lenses before 4b05bf6; tdd-build.js accepted a self-reported PASS before ffcd8ae; unit.js/lib/converge.js accepted non-executed acceptance evidence before 0a4270f. Every one of those tests exists only as a transcript command. ~/.claude/workflows has no CI, no pre-commit hook, and no test runner, so the next edit to pev.js can silently reinstate the vacuous-quantifier bug and nothing anywhere will notice - the proof does not survive the session that produced it. This is the concrete form of "enforce in runtime, not policy": the code was fixed and the ENFORCEMENT was not, and only the enforcement is what makes the fix durable. Check: for every fix, name the automatic path that will re-run its discriminating test; if the answer is "I ran it", the item is not done.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A brief must specify the QUESTION and its acceptance criterion, not the verification METHOD; a coordinator-chosen method carries a blind spot the coordinator cannot see, and the executor must be authorised to overrule it Measured 2026-08-15/16 (session 817d0e1f), two independent instances in one session, both caught only because the executing agent overruled the brief. (1) I instructed an agent to verify workflow-script integrity with `node --check`; on files that mix ES-module export with a top-level return, node --check exits 0 even with `const x = (((;` appended - the prescribed method cannot fail, so it would have certified corrupted files (FM-287). (2) I specified measuring CI queue delay at RUN level; GitHub sets run_started_at ~= created_at, making run-level queue delay identically zero by construction, which would have inverted the ARC runner-sizing conclusion to "no warm pools needed" (FM-291). In both cases the QUESTION was sound and the METHOD was vacuous, and the vacuity was invisible to the author precisely because he chose the method for its plausibility. Checks: (a) briefs state the question plus what a PASS and a FAIL must each look like, leaving method to the executor; (b) any prescribed method ships with a positive control - show the method failing on a known-bad input before trusting it on the real one; (c) executors are told explicitly that overruling a method whose blind spot they can demonstrate is expected behaviour, not scope creep.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: An acceptance runner that strips a background-guard shim from PATH must re-arm the guard for the ITEM command, or genuinely backgrounded work escapes refusal and reports exit 0 fleet PR #558: cmd_acceptance stripped */cli-dispatch-bg-guard.* from PATH so run_one_check would resolve the real setsid, but BACKGROUND_GUARD_DIR was unset in the fresh process, so item commands also got real setsid/nohup. PoC: --item "esc=setsid bash -c 'sleep 19; echo leaked' &" returned {"exit_code":0} while the work kept running in a new session/pgid; bg_reap_process_group only reaps the check's own pgid. A false zero in the very mechanism that decides whether anything is green. In-group nohup was correctly refused with 45, which is what made the escape look safe. Found by cross-vendor review (Grok) after CI green and coordinator-executed acceptance both passed.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A review lane's GitHub identity must match its harness, and it must fail closed rather than borrow an ambient token, or cross-vendor independence becomes unverifiable fleet #560: a --harness grok review lane posted its VERDICT comment as psimmons-claude-worker. The review was genuinely Grok's (12.6KB of Grok analysis, findings correct) but the identity was Claude's. The merge gate requires a named reviewer of a different vendor than the builder, and the only durable externally-checkable part of that evidence is the comment author -- so a Grok review of a Claude-built PR reads to any later auditor as Claude reviewing Claude (FM-282). rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A lane that completes its work but cannot commit must report a status distinct from 'the agent failed', naming the recoverable artifact fleet #555: a grok lane reported status=agent-failed, commits=0, exit 13 -- while the work was complete and correct (3 bats files, 762 lines, gate passing 41/41). A real outcome recorded as an absence.

rationale: filed at creation time

rationale: filed at creation time

rationale: filed at creation time

rationale: filed at creation time

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A review lane must be placed at the commit under review; if it is handed the base instead, reviewers either improvise a fetch or fail closed, and the refusal is indistinguishable from a defect 2026-08-16 fleet campaign: four review lanes were dispatched with --base origin/main. rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A guard implemented by shimming PATH catches only the idiomatic invocation; an absolute-path call bypasses it entirely fleet PR #558 closed the setsid process-group escape by arming the background guard for the item command, verified: --item "esc=setsid ... &" went from exit_code 0 with a live orphan to 45 with none. rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Acceptance gate defaults to a hardcoded checkout, so every in-lane run tests the coordinator's tree instead of the agent's A dispatch acceptance gate resolved the tree under test as REPO=${1:-/home/psimmons/projects/fleet}. cli-dispatch stages the check script OUTSIDE the worktree and invokes it with NO argument, so the default won every in-lane run and the gate inspected the coordinator's UNFIXED main checkout rather than the agent's worktree. The gate reported check-failed for a CORRECT implementation twice in a row (fleet#540 attempt 1 and its retry); those two failures looked like a same-class IMPLEMENTATION failure and would have triggered a vendor switch under the loop cap, spending a second lane to re-fail against the same broken gate. Verified directly: with the worktree passed as an argument the script exits 0; with no argument, from inside that worktree, it exits 1 at the first probe. The implementation satisfied the positive control, all 8 direct behaviour probes, and 21 bats cases. SIGNATURE: a check runnable BOTH by a coordinator and inside a lane must resolve its target from its own cwd, never a default path, and must refuse loudly with a distinct non-zero exit when it cannot locate the tree - a gate that cannot find its own tree must never be able to report a pass. The direction here was fail-CLOSED, the only reason it was survivable; the identical defect in a gate whose default tree already satisfies the property fails OPEN and silently passes every broken implementation. DIAGNOSTIC LESSON: two consecutive same-class lane failures must be classified impl-caused vs gate-caused BEFORE the loop cap's method change is applied, because the cap's prescribed remedy (switch vendor) is exactly wrong for a gate-caused failure. Second occurrence of this shape in one session - the same hardcoded-path defect was caught pre-dispatch in the fleet#516 adversarial probe, where it would have made a lane test the coordinator's tree instead of its own.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Verification command in a dispatch brief was unsatisfiable, so it would have 'proved' the guard works regardless of truth A coordinator brief told a verifier to prove a new contract test guards a vendor patch by reverting the patch and running: ./dispatch/test/run-suite.sh --filter codex-evidence dispatch/test/codex-evidence-contract.bats -- expecting a non-zero exit as proof the guard fires. bats --filter matches TEST NAMES, not files, and no test in that file is named 'codex-evidence', so the filter selected ZERO tests and the runner exited 1 unconditionally. The command therefore returns 'guard fired' whether the guard works, is broken, or does not exist - the intended RED and the vacuous RED are indistinguishable. Confirmed directly afterward: FILTER_EXIT=1 with zero cases selected. The verifier noticed the mismatch and substituted a real proof (revert to the pre-patch backup, observe 4 specific red cases fail while both positive controls still pass), which is the only reason a vacuous result was not banked as evidence that the fleet-owned half of the item was sound. SIGNATURE: a check whose FAILURE mode is indistinguishable from its SUCCESS mode proves nothing, and a selector that silently matches nothing is the commonest way to build one. Any command used as proof-of-red must first be shown to select a non-empty set, and must be distinguishable from the empty-selection case - print the selected count, or assert the expected number of executed cases, never just the exit code. Same family as a green suite whose assertions never ran: the exit code is trusted while the population it ran over is unexamined. Note the direction: this one fails CLOSED into a FALSE POSITIVE - it manufactures evidence that a guard works, which is more dangerous than a missed defect because it terminates further checking.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Full suite fails while the executed-case count INCREASES, so a count-vs-base floor sees no regression fleet#540: acceptance gate green, but ./dispatch/test/run-suite.sh --jobs 4 gave HEAD EXIT=1 CASES=1601 FAILED=1 against BASE EXIT=0 CASES=1598 FAILED=0. The count went UP by 3 because the change added tests, while a DIFFERENT pre-existing test broke. The campaign's standard floor 'executed count >= base' is satisfied (1601 >= 1598) and therefore blind: it can only detect deletion of cases, never breakage of them. Only the runner EXIT CODE and the not-ok count caught it. The broken test was 'audition: the per-root lock does not suppress a protected transaction failure' (lifecycle-lock-scope.bats:271): audition_with_record_lock began swallowing a non-zero status from the function it protects, so a failed transaction reported success to its caller - a false green inside a lock wrapper that many callers inherit. SIGNATURE: count-based conservation checks and pass/fail checks are ORTHOGONAL and neither substitutes for the other; a PR that adds tests can hide a regression from a count floor indefinitely. Any gate asserting 'count >= base' must ALSO assert exit==0 and failed==0 at both commits, and must report all four numbers. Second-order lesson: the acceptance gate ran only the 21-case file the feature touched and was green, so a gate passing is not a suite passing - scope the acceptance run to the whole suite before merge, not to the feature's own file.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Consistency check SKIPS when its lookup key is absent, so the very edit it polices disarms it fleet#566: tests/test_static_calibration_gate.py verifies 'if data/task-calibration.jsonl has a row for this hash, it must match live scores'. The hash is computed over the task TREE, so ANY edit inside the task tree changes the hash, removes the matching row, and makes the check SKIP rather than fail - 'skipped: registry has no row for current linkvault hash yet'. Demonstrated with a PURE COMMENT change (fixing two stale fixture docstrings): before the edit 'Ran 94 tests / OK', after 'Ran 94 tests / OK (skipped=1)'. Verified both directions by stashing the edit and re-running. The executed-case count is IDENTICAL at 94, so a count-vs-base floor cannot see the disarming either. The check exists to catch a task tree drifting from its registered calibration, and the mechanism that signals drift is the mechanism that suppresses the check - a real logic change moving the floor from 13 would produce the identical green. SIGNATURE: absence of a lookup key must not be inferred as 'nothing to check'; absence is also exactly what a regression looks like. A check that cannot evaluate its predicate must FAIL, with a distinct signal, never skip. If a legitimate state genuinely lacks the key (a brand-new task before first calibration) that state must be represented EXPLICITLY - a marker, an allowlist, a 'pending' band - never inferred from absence. Near-identical prior art in this corpus: hc-FM-217, where modules that failed to import were collected into an 'unresolved' warn list and excluded from the comparison, leaving an empty collision set that printed PASS.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Four fix rounds each tightened the comparison while the tokenizer stayed narrow, so the bypass just moved fleet#516/#565: a guard against citing the wrong calibration gate went through four build rounds, each reviewed by an independent cross-vendor reviewer, each shipping GREEN and each bypassed a different way. R1/R2 were a blacklist of phrasings (any natural rewrite slipped past; cap hit, method changed). R3 inverted the rule to deny-by-default with a small permit set, but the permit test compared value MEMBERSHIP not shape, so 13/13/13 duplicated, 18/13 truncated and 23/18/13 reordered all passed. R4 compared exact shape/order/cardinality - and 13/18/23/29 then produced ZERO citation groups, because GROUP_RE's {1,2} quantifier plus a (?![\w/]) lookahead means an overlong run matches nothing at all. Critically 11/17/23/29 - the ORIGINAL WRONG GATE with a fourth value appended - became invisible: not permitted-too-generously, but never surfaced to the permit logic at all. SIGNATURE: every round hardened the JUDGE while leaving the RECOGNIZER narrow, and a candidate the recognizer never emits cannot be judged by any rule however strict. When successive fixes to a validator keep failing in NEW ways rather than repeating, suspect the extraction/tokenization stage rather than the decision stage: widen recognition FIRST, then tighten permits. Process lesson: a declared stopping rule set BEFORE the round (split the PR rather than run round five) is what stopped the loop; the verified factual correction was landed separately and the unconverged guard moved to its own issue rather than holding it hostage.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Reviewer conflated two distinct claims sharing a numeric signature and filed a HIGH that would have INTRODUCED an error fleet PR#564: an independent reviewer returned VERDICT fail with a HIGH finding that routing/README.md:79 cited '0-of-2 = 11/23, 1-of-2 = 17/23' for r3-linkvault-v1 and must be corrected to 13/18/23 to match the registered gate. Measured live rather than argued: static_calibration.py reports the FIXTURES score 13/18/23, so the registry half of the finding was right - but that documentation line describes OBSERVED MODEL SCORES, not the fixture calibration gradient. It is immediately followed by 'Measured actor profile (n=6/cell...)' and its bullets bind 11 and 17 to named model families, corroborated by the round-3 evidence FINDINGS.md. Applying the requested fix would have replaced a TRUE statement about what models scored with a FALSE one. SIGNATURE: two semantically different claims that share a numeric signature (here a 3-value gradient) will be conflated by a reviewer pattern-matching on the numbers, and the resulting correction is an OVER-correction - strictly worse than the miss, because it manufactures a fresh falsehood inside a document whose purpose is evidence, and it arrives wearing the authority of a review. Mitigation that worked: refuse to act on any citation finding until the claim TYPE is established by measurement, and dispatch a second independent reviewer explicitly tasked with attacking the refutation rather than re-reviewing the diff, since the party who wrote the refutation must not be the party who closes it out. Note the same review's MEDIUM finding was real and led to hc-FM for fleet#566 - a wrong headline finding is not a worthless review.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Changing what a lane DELIVERS invalidated the gate that CONSUMES it, so the gate failed every compliant lane A founder ruling (2026-08-16) changed the delivery contract for third-party changes: agents must commit a PATCH FILE into the repo instead of live-editing an installed plugin. The rework brief was updated accordingly and the lane complied exactly - it delivered dispatch/vendor-patches/codex-1.0.6-fleet-263.patch plus 498 lines of bats and left the installed plugin untouched, verified by mtime. But the ACCEPTANCE GATE was not updated: it still probed the INSTALLED plugin root. So it reported check-failed on all four fail-open probes, and its own summary line said 'NOT enforced by the installed plugin' - accurate about the thing it looked at, and irrelevant to the thing that was delivered. A perfectly compliant lane was scored as a failure, and the harness would have scored every future compliant lane the same way. SIGNATURE: an acceptance gate is one half of a delivery CONTRACT; changing what the producer emits without changing what the checker consumes leaves the checker silently validating the wrong artifact. Whenever a brief's deliverable shape changes - file instead of in-place edit, patch instead of commit, artifact instead of side effect - the gate must be re-pointed in the SAME change, and its discrimination re-proved against the new artifact. Note the failure direction: this one failed CLOSED (a good lane looked bad), which is survivable and self-announcing. The mirror case is a gate still pointed at a location where the property already holds, which fails OPEN and passes every broken lane silently. Third gate defect of this session in the same family - see the hardcoded-checkout gate and the unsatisfiable proof-of-red; the recurring root is that gates were written against an assumed artifact location and never re-verified against the real one.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A parked PR disposition rotted in BOTH directions and would have frozen the work indefinitely on an expired premise fleet PR#548 carried a parked disposition recording (a) a hold because it 'depends on fleet#386 by its own issue text' and (b) a fail-open-validator blocker marked SAME_CLASS_REPEAT, which under the loop cap forbids a third same-method attempt. Re-adjudicated at the unchanged head 5ecd9aa on 2026-08-16: BOTH were false. #386 had CLOSED on 2026-08-10, satisfying the dependency. The fail-open blocker was not reproducible - every gate the PR names fails CLOSED when starved: absent input -> jq -e exit 2 and sha256sum -c exit 1; empty -> exit 4 / exit 1; malformed -> exit 5 / exit 1 / run_cmd exact-match exit 97. Because a SAME_CLASS_REPEAT verdict forbids re-attempt, the stale park was self-sealing: the very disposition that was wrong was also the reason nobody would re-test it, so it would have frozen the work indefinitely. The real blocker was something the park had never identified at all (see below). SIGNATURE: a parked disposition is a CLAIM WITH A TIMESTAMP, not a standing fact - it is evidence about a head at a moment, and both the world (dependencies closing) and the code can move underneath it. Re-verify a park before acting on it, in BOTH directions: it can be too pessimistic (blocking landable work) as well as too optimistic. The danger is asymmetric for terminal-sounding labels like SAME_CLASS_REPEAT, PARKED or REFUTE, which suppress the re-testing that would expose them; those need an explicit expiry or a re-verify-before-citing rule. Corollary observed in the same adjudication: parked dispositions record the blocker that was FOUND, not the blocker that MATTERS, so re-adjudication must re-derive from acceptance criteria rather than only re-checking the recorded findings.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Restore verified against a snapshot taken FROM the modified thing, proving stability and mistaken for pristineness A dispatch lane live-edited an installed plugin outside its repo. The coordinator backed up the modified files, later restored from that backup, compared md5sums, saw them match, and reported 'plugin restored, md5-verified / installed plugin unchanged' - repeatedly and confidently, to the founder. The comparison was structurally incapable of showing what was claimed: the backup was taken AFTER the modification, so backup == installed proves only that the state was STABLE between the two reads, never that it was PRISTINE. Measured: vendor git HEAD 88d8dee vs backup 9f12e7b vs installed 9f12e7b - backup and installed agreed with each other and BOTH differed from the only provenance-bearing baseline. An independent reviewer caught it while checking an unrelated scope rule; the coordinator's own repeated verification never could have. Compounding error: the backup covered only the files that session happened to touch, not the full diff-vs-baseline, so a third modified file (codex-companion.mjs, carrying a DIFFERENT closed issue's live fix) was never snapshotted and was nearly destroyed by the obvious remediation. SIGNATURE: a restore/integrity check must compare against a PROVENANCE-BEARING baseline - git HEAD, a package checksum, a signed artifact, an upstream re-download - never against a snapshot derived from the artifact under test. Snapshot-vs-snapshot answers 'did it change since I looked?' and is routinely misread as 'is it as it should be?'. Determine the backup's provenance BEFORE trusting it as a restore point, and define the backup set from the full diff against the baseline, not from the subset you believe you modified. Same family as verifying a config against its documentation rather than against the running system.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Build lanes dispatched without --no-pr minted three duplicate PRs the coordinator then had to close Across one campaign session the coordinator dispatched build lanes with cli-dispatch start and omitted --no-pr three times (fleet #567, #571, #572). Each lane opened its own PR on its dispatch/<task> branch as soon as it delivered, before the coordinator had verified anything. All three had to be closed as duplicates of the PR the coordinator opened deliberately, and each duplicate carried a commit authored cli-dispatch@localhost, which resolves to NO GitHub login and therefore could never have landed anyway (cli-dispatch land refuses exit 27 when it cannot determine the authoring login). Consequences beyond the noise: an open PR is a claim that work is ready for review, so three unreviewed lane outputs sat publicly labelled as proposals; and a reviewer or a queue-draining workflow could have adjudicated the duplicate instead of the real PR, wasting a full review round on a branch nobody intended to merge. SIGNATURE: a dispatch tool whose DEFAULT is to publish means every omitted suppression flag is an outbound action taken without a decision. When the coordinator intends to open the PR itself after verification, --no-pr is not optional decoration; it is what keeps publication gated on the verification step. Fix at the dispatch site, not by remembering: put --no-pr in the standing build-lane invocation template alongside --check-script and --check-strength, so omitting it is a visible deletion rather than a silent default. Same family as any tool that treats publication as the default rather than an explicit act.

rationale: filed at creation time

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Long-running background poller outlived its ambient GitHub App installation token 2026-08-18, PR#326 CI poll: a background poll loop inherited the shell's GH_TOKEN at spawn; App installation tokens expire (~1h), so after expiry every iteration returned 401 Bad credentials and the loop burned to TIMEOUT with total=null — the SHA-pinned gate reported failure that was pure auth rot, indistinguishable in the summary line from a real CI outcome until the log was read. evidence: catalog-guard's bin/tests/*.bats step is persistently red on main — needs sibling-repo checkout The catalog-guard workflow (.github/workflows/guard.yml) step 'Run bin/ tool bats tests (require-real-ci, land)' runs bats bin/tests/*.bats, which includes tests in bin/tests/test_add_failure_mode.bats that exercise the full canonical-add loop (extract_mechanical.py -> L2 regen -> reconcile) against sibling repos (fleet, claude-codex, fleet-dispatch) checked out as worktree siblings. Result: 8 of 237 cases fail every run (tests 8, 11-14, 19-21 -- canonical add's extract/L2/reconcile ordering, tier recording, POINTER.md/HIGH.md regen, dot-dot/symlink alias, real-reconciler loop, sibling shortfall, short-source rollback). Confirmed red on main at HEAD da72a3f and on the last 3 build-red-ci-pair runs and split-108-fail-loud (PR#124) -- pre-existing, not introduced by any of those branches. Fix: either check out the three sibling repos in guard.yml before the bin/tests step (mirroring how the split lane worked around it locally by symlinking fleet/claude-codex/fleet-dispatch into its job tmp dir), or scope bin/tests/*.bats the same declared-reduced-check way the reconcile step already is, with an explicit named list of what's unchecked in CI. Generalizable rule: a workflow step that silently needs repo-external state (sibling checkouts) will read green in a dev worktree with those siblings present and red in CI without disclosing why, unless the gap is declared inline like the reconcile step already models.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: tdd-build acceptance command scoped to one test file missed a real regression in a sibling file (recurrence of hc-FM-312 pattern) fleet PR#643 (#498 W3): the dispatched tdd-build item's acceptanceCmd ran only dispatch/test/root-launcher-wiring.bats (the feature's own test file), which the lane's implementer and the coordinator's own host-verification both used to certify the change. Neither caught that the new LANE_JOURNAL_FIELDS_JQ fields (origin_verification, origin_verification_reason) broke dispatch/test/lane-journal.bats:149, a SEPARATE pre-existing test in a different file that pins the journal row's exact closed key set as a literal sorted array. Fleet's own CI (which runs the full suite) caught it; a narrower acceptance command would not have. This is the same mechanism as hc-FM-312 (fleet#540: an acceptance gate scoped to the feature's own 21-case file was green while a DIFFERENT pre-existing test broke elsewhere in the suite) -- second occurrence of this exact class in this repo, now against a hand-authored tdd-build acceptanceCmd rather than a --check-script gate. SIGNATURE: any acceptance command for a change that touches a shared, closed-set contract (a fixed key set, a fixed token vocabulary, a fixed schema) must run the FULL suite that contract lives in, not just the feature's own test file -- a closed-set assertion by definition lives outside the feature that adds a member to the set. Fix applied here: pinned test widened (dispatch/test/lane-journal.bats), re-verified against the full dispatch suite, re-pushed, re-gated. Going forward: when dispatching a tdd-build item whose implPaths touch a field/key/token that a DIFFERENT file's test enumerates as a closed set, the acceptanceCmd must include that file, not just the changed feature's own tests.
